page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.4xlarge is a dedicated virtual machine instance within the vendor's Big Data server family. It is driven by the x86_64 Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The server provisions 16 dedicated virtual CPUs and 64 GB of RAM, yielding an even distribution of 4.0 GB of memory per core. The underlying virtualization layer is managed via KVM, delivering dedicated CPU scheduling without contention from shared processor resources.

A primary differentiator for the ecs.d1.4xlarge is its bundled local storage array, offering 47,244 GB of hard disk drive space attached directly to the host. Unlike NVMe-backed configurations that target extreme IOPS, this massive magnetic storage capacity focuses on bulk sequential read and write operations. On the networking side, the instance delivers a baseline bandwidth of 6 Gbps, supporting steady node-to-node communication within clustered topologies without complimentary public IPv4 addressing included.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, pairing magnetic disk arrays with balanced compute and memory enables a cost-effective footprint for raw storage volume. Deployments avoid the high premium associated with high-capacity solid-state media when workloads are bounded by volume rather than microsecond latency. Consequently, the ecs.d1.4xlarge fits distributed big data frameworks such as Apache Hadoop, Apache Spark, distributed file systems, centralized log analytics, and extract, transform, and load pipelines.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.4xlarge is a big data instance designed for data-intensive processing and high-density sequential storage architectures. Powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz on an x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 16 dedicated vCPUs alongside 64 GB of system memory, maintaining a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Its core hardware feature is the inclusion of 47,244 GB of local hard disk drive (HDD) storage paired directly with the compute host. Network throughput is backed by a 6 Gbps baseline bandwidth allocation. Because the local storage relies on spinning disks, the configuration prioritizes high capacity and sequential throughput over random I/O operations. This resource profile offers cost efficiency for large data repositories that do not demand expensive solid-state media. The ecs.d1.4xlarge is suited for distributed big data processing, Apache Hadoop or Spark worker clusters, log retention systems, and batch ETL pipelines requiring large local disk buffers.
